Difference Between Star Delta and DOL Starter: Quick Reference Table

The difference between star delta and DOL starter is the voltage applied to the motor windings at start. A DOL starter applies full line voltage at once, while a star delta starter starts the motor in star, so each winding sees about 58 percent of line voltage, and then switches to delta.

PointDOL starterStar delta starter
Starting voltage per winding100 percent of line voltageAbout 58 percent (1/√3)
Starting current6 to 8 times full load currentAbout one third of DOL value
Starting torqueFull locked rotor torqueAbout 33 percent of DOL torque
ContactorsOneThree plus a timer
Motor leadsThreeSix
Overload relay settingMotor full load currentAbout 58 percent of full load current
Motor requirementAny induction motorDelta rated for running, six terminals
Typical useSmall motors, usually under 5 kWMedium to large motors on light starting loads

How to Decide in Three Checks

  1. Check whether the supply can accept 6 to 8 times full load current at start.
  2. Check whether the load can accelerate with only one third of normal starting torque.
  3. Check the nameplate for a delta running connection at the supply voltage.
